mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown four consecutive weeks of accelerating decline (-28.7 to -39.4). This momentum in foot-traffic reduction, driven by cumulative caution, is expected to persist for the next four weeks, pushing the mean RETAIL_REC further below its trailing 28-day average.
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days equals or exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, i.e., the decline halts or reverses.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week drop in PARKS exceeding 10 points reflects a sharp pullback in outdoor discretionary activity, which typically precedes a parallel contraction in retail and recreation visits within two weeks as consumers broadly reduce non-essential outings.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week decline exceeds 10 percentage points (as observed t-1w to t-0w: -7.6 to -19.9)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 12.3 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 2 weeks does not decline relative to the prior 2-week mean despite the PARKS threshold being crossed.

mechanism_narrative: Joint declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate reduced commuting and associated incidental shopping (lunch breaks, after-work errands). When both series fall together by comparable magnitudes, the compounded loss of commute-linked footfall drives a larger RETAIL_REC decline than either series alone would predict.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fell by roughly 9-12 points between t-2w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further over the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both continue to decline jointly.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous decline across RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and PARKS alongside rising RESIDENTIAL resembles a policy-driven tightening response to a resurgence (e.g., renewed advisories or capacity limits). Under such a regime, RETAIL_REC is expected to keep falling until the regime shifts toward reopening.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 1.9 to 3.0 while all other categories fell
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 4 weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, indicating the tightening-regime mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-to-late August typically brings a seasonal back-to-school shopping uptick that temporarily boosts RETAIL_REC regardless of broader mobility trends. This seasonal demand should produce a short, one-week partial rebound in RETAIL_REC before the underlying downward trend reasserts.
candidate_trigger: calendar period falls within the two weeks preceding typical regional school-start dates (mid-to-late August)
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-08-15 falls within typical back-to-school shopping window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no week-over-week uptick during the back-to-school window and instead continues its monotonic decline.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has declined far less steeply than RETAIL_REC (-18.1 vs -39.4 at t-0w), indicating consumers are preserving essential trips while cutting discretionary ones. This divergence signals a substitution behavior that will keep discretionary RETAIL_REC suppressed relative to essential categories over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC decline magnitudes exceeds 15 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:t-0w gap between GROCERY_PHARM (-18.1) and RETAIL_REC (-39.4) is 21.3 points
failure_condition: The gap between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC narrows (RETAIL_REC recovers toward GROCERY_PHARM levels) while the threshold condition is active.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in the weekly declines of PARKS and TRANSIT, both more than doubling their prior-week drop, signals a sudden, broad-based retreat from public mobility that will feed through to a sharp one-week drop in RETAIL_REC as outdoor leisure and transit-enabled errands collapse together.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 12.3 points and TRANSIT fell 4.3 points between t-1w and t-0w, both accelerating from the prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not show an accelerated one-week decline matching the combined acceleration seen in PARKS and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility falls below -35 points, a level consistent with renewed remote-work mandates, this signals an active policy-driven reduction in in-person economic activity that will suppress RETAIL_REC for the following four weeks until WORKPLACES mobility recovers above that threshold.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -35 percentage points (observed at t-0w: -39.7)
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -39.7 at t-0w, below the -35 threshold
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining below -35, or RETAIL_REC continues to fall even after WORKPLACES recovers above -35.
